draft: Pruning at our orchard runs across Saturday and Sunday in January, 9.30 until dusk on both days. If this is your first pruning day, bring stout boots, a warm coat, thick work mitts and a flask; saws, pruning hooks and standing stools stay in our tool hut, so you do not lug any of that along. Marion, who runs our pruning days, says that anybody worrying about doing it wrong should stop worrying, as a first cut is hardly a fatal cut. Autumn fruit is split in thirds: a third to local folk who put in a day's work, a third to our autumn juicing day, and a third to our community food bank.

Anyone with a mobility need can arrange a lift right up to the main door: a car may pull into the drop-off bay at the front, or a call ahead to the reception hall will bring out a porter with a chair. When the sound drops away, moving three or four rows forward cures it most of the time, and if it does not, the duty steward can reset the amplifier in the cupboard beside the stage.

The path will lie under water from one hour up to the peak, and for one hour afterward. At that time, take the inland lane by the old chapel, along the field edge, and back down the church track, which will add roughly a mile to the walk. Robin, who kept the tide log here for a decade, warned the walking club that nobody had ever been caught out by the water, only by the clock.

draft: Any member may take six packets each spring, writing a name, the bed number and the variety in the ledger by the trestle table. Every packet here has been raised within three miles, which means the seed meets the same wet clay and the same late chills each year, unlike a packet that arrives by mail. draft: The kit-lending scheme runs like this at the bench. Begin at the entry desk, where a member card is checked and a slip is filled in with the item, the date lent and the date due back. Then take the item away and keep it a full week, and, when extra time is needed, ring the bench and renew it; a single renewal buys seven extra days. When the item is handed back, a bench member checks it there and then, and if all is well the fifteen is returned that minute. Finally, when it returns damaged, say as much when handing it in: the pledge is held while the repair is priced, the charge is capped at the pledge, and plain wear is wiped.

draft: Begin the moment you see the cluster: come inside, shut the windows next to it, then bring pets in. Give them room, ten feet or so, since bees in flight will simply veer wide. Next, note where they sit, how high off the ground, plus the time they settled; the responder will need it. Then ring the club officer, who keeps the beekeeper register, before dusk, since the cluster will move by night. Never hit them, never wet them, never use insecticide: bees resting like this hold no interest in you, but knock them free plus they will defend themselves. One thing more: if they slip inside brickwork, ring while they still cluster: hidden bees will need the front opened up.
